title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 164
paragraphs: This Cadmus, before these events, had inherited from his father the government of Cos in a prosperous state; and, under no compulsion or threat of danger but moved simply by uprightness of character, he had voluntarily placed the government in the hands of the people of Cos and departed to Sicily, where he took the city of Zancle (which had changed its name to Messene) from the Samians and colonized it anew. This Cadmus, having come there in the manner described, Gelon was now sending, having picked him out because of the integrity he had found in him in other matters. In addition to his other honorable actions, Cadmus left this deed to be remembered — and not the least of them. Having charge of that great sum of money that Gelon had entrusted to him, though he might easily have taken it for himself, he did not choose to do so; but when the Greeks had prevailed in the sea-fight and Xerxes had withdrawn and gone home, he too returned to Sicily bringing back the entire sum with him.
